base_properties.human_readable: Tiered Mobility Rights and Contributory Welfare Access in Federal Unions

perspectives.label: The Economically Inactive Mobile Person
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 1: ECONOMICALLY INACTIVE MOBILE PERSON (SNARE) — Structurally trapped by tiering logic. Free movement in law conflicts with welfare access restrictions in practice. Cannot exit: return to origin state may be financially inaccessible; cannot meet contribution requirements in destination state without employment; cannot establish residency to accumulate contribution history without proving self-sufficiency first. Circular enforcement mechanism creates maximum experienced extraction with minimal coordination benefit. No voice in welfare policy design.

perspectives.label: The Low-Contribution Worker
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 2: LOW-CONTRIBUTION WORKER (TANGLED ROPE) — Experiences genuine coordination (access to expanded labor market) alongside asymmetric extraction (tiered benefits, welfare gatekeeping, precarious status). Can exit by returning home or relocating, but exit cost is high (wage loss, family separation, credential non-recognition). Benefits from cross-border mobility for employment search, but welfare tiering extracts via benefit denial and conditional residency. Some agency — can accumulate contributions over time — but not full mobility. Moderately organized in labor unions but with limited political voice over welfare policy.

perspectives.label: The High-Contribution Employed Member
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 3: HIGH-CONTRIBUTION EMPLOYED MEMBER (ROPE) — Pure coordination benefit from tiering logic. Free movement enables labor market matching; contribution-based access aligns benefit access with tax contribution. Experiences the constraint as coordination: tiering ensures they are not cross-subsidizing inactive persons; their contributions accumulate into portable welfare claims. Can arbitrage across states (seek employment in high-wage jurisdictions, accumulate benefits, port them home). Net beneficiary — extraction flows toward them, not from them.

perspectives.label: The Member State Welfare Administrator
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 4: MEMBER STATE WELFARE ADMINISTRATOR (TANGLED ROPE) — Experiences coordination (tiering logic allows states to protect welfare system fiscal capacity) alongside extraction (must enforce gatekeeping rules, manage residency verification, police contribution history). Genuinely benefits from tiering: prevents fiscal shocks from unexpected inflows of inactive persons. But also bears cost: administrative complexity, legal liability for welfare denials, political exposure to human rights challenges. Constrained by federal law requirements for non-discrimination in employment but retains closure authority in welfare access. High power within member state, but constrained at federal level.

perspectives.label: The Federal Economic Policy Framework
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 5: FEDERAL ECONOMIC POLICY FRAMEWORK (ROPE) — Pure coordination from the federal policy level. Tiering logic enables simultaneous achievement of three coordination goals: (1) labor market integration through free movement, (2) welfare system protection through contribution-based access, (3) fiscal sustainability through gatekeeping. The framework arbitrages between mobility rights and welfare boundaries, treating both as legitimate policy goals. No extraction from this perspective — the framework sees tiering as the coordinating solution to competing valid objectives.

perspectives.label: The Human Rights Authority (Analytical Degradation)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 6: HUMAN RIGHTS AUTHORITY / ANALYTICAL OBSERVER (PITON) — Views tiering as degraded coordination masking extraction. The formal principle ('free movement + contribution-based welfare') obscures operational reality: tier walls prevent most mobility in practice, and contribution-history requirements lock persons into dependency states. Theater ratio high: tiering appears as technical administrative rationality but functions as coercive status differentiation. The human rights framework sees the constraint as inertial — persisting through institutional compliance theater rather than functional necessity. From a civilizational perspective, tiering naturalizes economic status into legal personhood (mobile employed vs immobile inactive), but this is a constructed institutional choice, not inherent to federation logic.

omegas.question: Does the contribution-history requirement operationally identify persons who are net fiscal contributors, or does it function as a pretextual device for status differentiation?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Longitudinal fiscal analysis: compare lifetime tax contribution vs cumulative benefit access for cohorts meeting vs not meeting tiering thresholds; decompose actual contribution dynamics from formal accumulation requirements
omegas.impact: If contribution history accurately predicts net contribution: tiering is technically justified (Rope classification from administrative perspective gains legitimacy). If pretextual: tiering is extraction mechanism (Snare classification from inactive perspective is operational reality). Classification could shift to pure Snare if contribution thresholds systematically exclude vulnerable populations independent of fiscal outcomes.
omegas.description: Whether contribution requirements operationally identify fiscal contributions or function as status gatekeeping

omegas.question: Do welfare access restrictions create circular dependency: cannot establish residency without self-sufficiency proof, cannot prove self-sufficiency without welfare access, cannot accumulate contributions without residency status?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Case-level analysis of residency grant denials and welfare access disputes; mapping of actual pathway sequences for inactive persons attempting to establish status; identification of structural bottlenecks vs administrative discretion
omegas.impact: If circular: constraint functions as pure trapping mechanism (Snare from inactive perspective is structural, not just experienced). If pathways exist: moderate extraction (Tangled Rope from inactive perspective is accurate). Classification of powerless perspective hinges on this — full circularity = trapped exit option; partial pathways = constrained exit option.
omegas.description: Whether residency/welfare/contribution requirements create circular entrapment

omegas.question: Does tiering actually protect member state welfare systems from fiscal shock, or is welfare disruption primarily driven by factors orthogonal to contribution history (aging, automation, fiscal austerity)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Fiscal decomposition analysis comparing welfare system pressures in high-mobility vs low-mobility scenarios, holding benefit levels constant; attribution analysis for welfare system disruptions by causal driver (demographic shift, labor market change, policy choice, migration patterns)
omegas.impact: If tiering materially protects welfare systems: the Rope classification from administrator perspective is functionally justified. If orthogonal drivers dominate: tiering is theater — welfare protection rationale is secondary to status boundary maintenance (shifts to Piton classification). If tiering worsens fiscal capacity (by excluding workers who would contribute): tiering is counterproductive extraction (shifts toward Snare).
omegas.description: Whether tiering actually protects welfare systems or merely provides cover for status differentiation

omegas.question: Is the selective-solidarity reading (contribution-based tiering) structurally necessary for managing tension between mobility and welfare, or do alternative readings (integration-primary: mutual citizenship, member-sovereignty-primary: closure authority) offer equivalent or superior solutions?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative institutional analysis: model outcomes under each reading's operating principles; empirical comparison with alternative federal systems (US labor mobility + state welfare variation, Canada internal mobility + benefit portability, Switzerland contribution-based canton access); identification of distributional consequences and Pareto-feasible alternatives
omegas.impact: If selective-solidarity is Pareto-superior: the reading instantiates optimal institutional design (validates Tangled Rope as appropriate classification). If alternative readings achieve equivalent mobility/fiscal goals with different distributional impact: the reading choice reflects power distribution among reading holders, not technical necessity (shifts framing from institutional rationality to political choice). This omega directly addresses the kernel contest and committer structure.
omegas.description: Whether selective-solidarity is structurally necessary or reflects political choice among alternative readings

omegas.question: What constitutes 'economically inactive' for tiering purposes? Are students, caregivers, disabled persons, retirees, and job-seekers treated uniformly or with status-specific provisions? How does the operational definition diverge from formal eligibility?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Administrative code analysis and case-law review: map formal categories vs operational enforcement; identify which inactive statuses receive presumptive welfare access vs gatekeeping; determine whether inactivity definitions change with labor market conditions or welfare fiscal pressure
omegas.impact: If definition is rigid and uniform: tiering produces predictable distributional outcomes. If definition is flexible and context-dependent: enforcement becomes discretionary, and experienced suppression (and chi) varies with administrative choice and economic cycle. High discretion shifts classification toward Snare from inactive perspective (suppression increases as enforcement tightens during fiscal stress).
omegas.description: How 'economically inactive' is operationally defined and whether definitions change with context

omegas.question: This constraint instantiates the 'selective_solidarity' reading of the federation_membership_obligations kernel. How does this reading relate structurally to the sibling readings 'integration_primary' and 'member_sovereignty_primary'? What core commitments differentiate this reading from alternatives?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Committer-axis analysis: explicit declaration of foundational axioms that define selective-solidarity relative to siblings; identification of which axioms would need to be overridden to adopt alternative readings; tracking of how each reading's core premise appears in the constraint's beneficiary/victim structure, enforcement mechanism, and theta values
omegas.impact: Determines whether selective-solidarity is a live held position or analytically derived category. If live: constraint reflects actual political choice by actors holding this reading. If derived: constraint represents what selective-solidarity logic implies if adopted, but may not reflect current political equilibrium. Affects interpretation of perspectival gaps — are they observations of different readings being held simultaneously, or artifacts of analytical decomposition?
omegas.description: Kernel reading contest structure and definitional axioms of selective-solidarity reading

commentary.narrative_context: The tiering of free movement rights by contribution history and economic activity status represents a structural compromise between supranational mobility rights and member-state welfare system protection. This constraint instantiates the 'selective_solidarity' reading of the federation_membership_obligations kernel — a commitment to distribute federation benefits and obligations according to demonstrated economic contribution rather than citizenship status alone or unconditional mobility rights alone. The constraint creates a bifurcated legal status for mobile persons: employed workers with sufficient contribution history access both free movement and portable welfare benefits, while economically inactive persons face restricted movement rights and gatekept welfare access. This reading competes with two sibling readings: the 'integration_primary' reading emphasizes that free movement is constitutive of federal citizenship and single-market functioning, requiring welfare system adaptation to mobility; the 'member_sovereignty_primary' reading emphasizes that member states retain closure authority to protect welfare system sustainability. The selective-solidarity reading attempts to reconcile these by making both free movement and welfare closure conditional on contribution status. The constraint exhibits Tangled Rope characteristics: genuine coordination function (enables labor market matching while protecting welfare fiscal capacity) alongside asymmetric extraction (tiering creates permanent underclasses of inactive persons with restricted rights). Base extractiveness has risen from 0.35 to 0.58 over the measurement interval, reflecting administrative tightening of contribution requirements and elaboration of gatekeeping mechanisms. Suppression has increased from 0.45 to 0.68, indicating rising enforcement machinery and declining exit alternatives for inactive persons.
key_agents: Economically Inactive Mobile Persons: Primary victim (powerless/trapped) — experience circular gatekeeping logic preventing welfare access, residency establishment, and status accumulation
Low-Contribution Workers: Secondary victim (moderate/constrained) — benefit from mobility for employment but face tiered benefit access and precarious status
High-Contribution Employed Members: Primary beneficiary (institutional/arbitrage) — net beneficiaries of tiering logic; can arbitrage across jurisdictions and accumulate portable benefits
Member State Welfare Administrators: Secondary beneficiary (organized/constrained) — benefit from tiering protection of welfare system fiscal capacity but bear enforcement costs and legal liability
Federal Economic Policy Framework: Coordinating authority (organized/arbitrage) — treats tiering as solution enabling simultaneous achievement of mobility and fiscal protection goals
Human Rights Authority: Analytical observer (institutional/analytical) — views tiering as degraded coordination masking status-based extraction; identifies theater in administrative rationality
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.58): Moderate-high and rising. The base measurement reflects that tiering extracts meaningful benefits for high-contribution workers (access expansion, benefit portability) and for administrators (fiscal control) while imposing costs on inactive and low-contribution persons (status restrictions, benefit denial). The metric is not higher because genuine coordination function exists — the system does enable expanded labor market access and does protect welfare fiscal capacity from unmanaged inflows. But the extraction is substantial because cost distribution is asymmetric and exit options are severely constrained for the inactive. Rising trajectory (0.35 → 0.58) reflects administrative tightening: contribution thresholds have become more stringent, residency verification more invasive, and burden-of-proof has shifted to claimants to demonstrate self-sufficiency. Suppression (0.68): Moderate-high and rising. Structural barriers include residency requirements (cannot establish residency without self-sufficiency proof), contribution accumulation locks (cannot meet thresholds without employment), and information asymmetries (welfare eligibility rules are complex and often non-transparent). Informal suppression includes administrative discretion in welfare decisions, stigma attached to benefit claims, and network effects (isolated inactive persons have fewer information sources about rights). Rising suppression reflects both tightening enforcement and declining informal pathways (welfare administrators increasingly require formal documentation, reducing reliance on informal patronage or community networks). Theater ratio (0.62): Moderate-high and rising. Tiering is presented as technical administrative rationality ('contribution-based access prevents moral hazard'), but the operational effect is status differentiation based on economic activity. The theater reflects: (a) formal neutrality (rules apply equally) masking substantive differentiation (economic-based status determines legal rights); (b) procedural complexity (contribution calculation, residency accumulation) creating appearance of technical necessity; (c) welfare-protection rationale that may be secondary to boundary-maintenance function. Rising trajectory reflects increasing elaboration of administrative mechanisms — the more formalized and bureaucratic the tiering system becomes, the higher the theater ratio.
commentary.perspectival_gap: This constraint demonstrates maximum perspectival divergence across the observation sites. The economically inactive person (powerless/trapped) sees pure extraction (Snare) — tiering creates circular gatekeeping preventing legal status establishment and welfare access, with no exit option available. The low-contribution worker (moderate/constrained) sees mixed coordination and extraction (Tangled Rope) — genuine benefit from expanded labor market access alongside meaningful cost from tiered benefit denial, with partial exit options (returning home, accumulating contributions). The high-contribution employed member (institutional/arbitrage) sees pure coordination (Rope) — tiering enables labor market matching and benefit portability with no experienced extraction. The administrator (organized/constrained) sees coordination with enforcement cost (Tangled Rope) — fiscal protection is genuine benefit, but gatekeeping and verification create administrative burden. The federal policy framework (organized/arbitrage) sees optimal solution (Rope) — tiering reconciles mobility and welfare objectives. The human rights observer (institutional/analytical) sees degraded coordination (Piton) — tiering is theater masking extraction, persisting through institutional inertia rather than functional necessity. The gap reflects that the same structural mechanism (contribution-based gatekeeping) produces starkly different outcomes depending on the agent's position in the contribution hierarchy.
commentary.directionality_logic: Directionality (d) for each perspective is derived from the agent's structural position in the contribution-based extraction flow. High-contribution workers have d ≈ 0.05 (beneficiary + arbitrage exit = low d → negative f(d) → negative χ, experiencing subsidy). Inactive persons have d ≈ 0.95 (victim + trapped exit = high d → f(d)≈1.42 → high χ, experiencing maximum extraction). Low-contribution workers have d ≈ 0.75 (victim + constrained exit = d between beneficiary and trapped, experiencing extraction but with partial agency). Administrators have d ≈ 0.40 (mixed position: beneficiary from fiscal protection, victim of enforcement burden; constrained exit because they can adjust enforcement but cannot unilaterally override the tiering system). The federal framework has d ≈ 0.15 (beneficiary from coordinating multiple objectives; arbitrage exit because it can shift between reading implementations). The human rights observer has d ≈ 0.72 (observer position analyzing the system, but meta-analytically trapped by seeing tiering as theater). These d values are NOT overridden — they follow from structural declarations without need for explicit directionality_overrides.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: KERNEL READING INSTANTIATION: This constraint resolves mandatrophy by explicitly instantiating ONE reading of the federation_membership_obligations kernel. The mandatrophy question is not 'which classification is correct?' but rather 'which reading of federation obligations are we operating under?' The selective-solidarity reading makes commitment that federation membership involves graduated solidarity obligations based on demonstrated contribution. This reading enables Tangled Rope classification at the system level because it achieves genuine coordination (labor market integration + welfare sustainability) while distributing costs asymmetrically. Alternative readings would produce different classification profiles: the integration_primary reading (treating free movement as unconditional federation right) would shift the framework perspective toward Rope and the administrator perspective toward Snare (administrators would see extraction without coordination benefit). The member_sovereignty_primary reading (treating member states as having welfare closure authority over federation law) would shift toward Rope at the administrator level. The selective-solidarity reading splits the difference, making free movement conditional on contribution status. This explains why the perspectival gap exists: not because observers disagree on facts, but because they hold different readings of what federation membership commits. The mandate is resolved by rendering the reading choice explicit.
commentary.kernel_context: This constraint instantiates the SELECTIVE_SOLIDARITY reading of the FEDERATION_MEMBERSHIP_OBLIGATIONS kernel. The kernel is the contested commitment about what obligations member states owe to mobile persons and what entitlements mobile persons possess within the federal system. The sibling readings are: (1) INTEGRATION_PRIMARY: Federal citizenship creates unconditional mobility rights; member-state welfare boundaries must adapt to accommodate mobile persons. (2) MEMBER_SOVEREIGNTY_PRIMARY: Member states retain closure authority over welfare access; federal mobility rights are conditional on labor-market functionality and welfare-system sustainability. (3) SELECTIVE_SOLIDARITY (this reading): Federation membership involves graduated solidarity obligations proportional to demonstrated economic contribution; free movement and welfare access are both conditional on contribution history and employment status. The structural delta of the selective-solidarity reading is: mobile workers are bifurcated into employed (holding contribution history) and inactive; cost-bearing is distributed by contribution status rather than citizenship alone; welfare boundaries are maintained by contribution gatekeeping rather than nationality gatekeeping. This reading is formalized in EU law (EU Directive 2004/38/EC provisions on economically inactive persons, Social Security Regulation 883/2004 contribution-based benefit portability). The sibling readings remain politically live: integration-primary is advocated by human rights organizations and mobility advocates; member-sovereignty-primary is advocated by welfare-state defenders and conservative national governments; selective-solidarity is the institutional compromise reflected in current EU law.

network.dual_formulation_note: This constraint is ONE READING of the federation_membership_obligations kernel. Two sibling readings instantiate different constraints with different ε values and perspectival profiles. All three stories are linked via network.affects_constraints to indicate they are competing interpretations of the same kernel. The selective-solidarity reading produces moderate-high extractiveness (0.58) because tiering achieves coordination alongside asymmetric cost distribution. Alternative readings would produce different theta profiles: integration-primary would show lower extractiveness (0.35-0.40) because unconditional mobility reduces gatekeeping; member-sovereignty-primary would show higher extractiveness (0.65-0.75) at the mobility-seeker perspective because closure authority implies stronger suppression. The three readings form a kernel family — each is a defensible instantiation of federation membership logic, and the constraint story models how one such reading manifests in policy and law.
